title: When Practice Becomes Too Predictable
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空例。実在の調査結果・医学的助言・法令・教授法の実証効果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: An imagined music teacher notices that several students can perform a short passage accurately whenever they begin at the first measure, yet struggle when asked to start somewhere in the middle.
sentences.ja: 架空の音楽教師は複数の生徒が最初の小節から始めれば短い一節を正確に演奏できるが途中から始めるよう求めると苦労すると気づく。

sentences.en: The students have devoted considerable time to rehearsing the piece, and their ability to perform it from beginning to end has improved steadily over several weeks.
sentences.ja: 生徒は曲の練習にかなりの時間を割き最初から最後まで演奏する力は数週間着実に向上してきた。

sentences.en: Rather than dismissing that progress, the teacher asks what the students' usual practice arrangements have allowed them to learn and what other abilities might require a different approach.
sentences.ja: その進歩を退けず、通常の練習方法で何を学べたか、他のどの能力に別の方法が必要かを問う。

sentences.en: She recognizes that a procedure which produces successful performance under familiar conditions does not necessarily prepare students to respond when the conditions of a performance change.
sentences.ja: 身近な条件で成功を生む手順が演奏条件の変化に対応する準備を必ずしもさせないと認識する。

sentences.en: During a lesson, the teacher asks students to identify recognizable sections of the piece and explain how each section relates to the musical patterns that precede and follow it.
sentences.ja: 授業で曲の認識可能な部分を特定し各部分が前後の音楽パターンにどう関係するか説明するよう求める。

sentences.en: Some students discover that the movements required at the beginning of one section are easier to recall when they have just completed the preceding section than when they attempt them in isolation.
sentences.ja: ある生徒は一部分冒頭に必要な動きは単独で試みるより前部分を終えた直後に思い出しやすいことに気づく。

sentences.en: Their teacher suggests that the earlier passage may have become a useful cue without the students consciously recognizing the extent to which their performance depends on it.
sentences.ja: 前の一節が有用な手がかりになり演奏がどれほど依存するか意識的に認識していない可能性を教師は示唆する。

sentences.en: The observation does not establish that every student's difficulty has the same cause, but it provides a starting point for investigating how their practice could become less dependent on one predictable sequence.
sentences.ja: 観察は全生徒の困難が同じ原因だと確定しないが練習を一つの予測可能順序に依存しにくくする方法を調べる出発点になる。

sentences.en: The teacher prepares several activities that require the students to begin at different points, identify transitions between sections, and explain how they would recover after an interruption.
sentences.ja: 教師は異なる箇所から開始し部分間の移行を特定し、中断後どう再開するか説明する複数活動を用意する。

sentences.en: However, she continues to provide opportunities to perform the entire piece, since dividing a musical work into smaller tasks cannot by itself develop every aspect of a coherent performance.
sentences.ja: しかし曲を小作業に分けるだけでは一貫した演奏の全側面を発達させられないため全曲を演奏する機会も続けて提供する。

sentences.en: The students consequently examine connections between the different activities rather than treating one form of practice as an automatic replacement for all the others.
sentences.ja: そこで一練習形式を他全ての自動的代替と扱わず異なる活動間のつながりを調べる。

sentences.en: They begin to discuss whether their growing familiarity with the piece is accompanied by a greater ability to respond to situations that have not occurred during their normal rehearsals.
sentences.ja: 曲へのなじみの増加が通常練習で起きなかった状況への対応力増加を伴うか議論し始める。

sentences.en: For a subsequent classroom exercise, the students imagine how the same distinction might apply to activities outside music, including language learning and the completion of mathematical problems.
sentences.ja: 以後の活動で言語学習や数学問題など音楽以外にも同じ区別がどう適用されるか想像する。

sentences.en: A learner who can answer a question in a familiar worksheet might discover that recognizing the relevant idea in an unfamiliar problem creates an additional challenge.
sentences.ja: 慣れたワークシートで答えられる学習者も未知の問題で関連概念を認識することが追加課題になると気づくかもしれない。

sentences.en: The class avoids claiming that this analogy establishes the effectiveness of a particular teaching technique for every learner or academic subject.
sentences.ja: 類推が全学習者や教科に特定教授技法の有効性を確立するとは主張しない。

sentences.en: Instead, it encourages students to formulate more specific questions about the kinds of performance that their chosen activities are intended to support.
sentences.ja: 代わりに選んだ活動が支えることを意図した成績の種類についてより具体的な問いを作るよう促す。

sentences.en: Practice serves different purposes, and its value cannot always be judged through the ease with which a person completes a repeated task under stable conditions.
sentences.ja: 練習は異なる目的に役立ち、その価値は安定条件下で反復課題を容易に終える度合いだけでは常に判断できない。

sentences.en: A familiar sequence can be an important foundation for learning while leaving some aspects of independent performance insufficiently developed.
sentences.ja: 身近な順序は学びの重要な基礎になる一方独立した遂行の一部を十分発達させないまま残すことがある。

sentences.en: A thoughtful learner therefore examines both the progress made through repetition and the situations in which that progress can be meaningfully applied.
sentences.ja: 思慮深い学習者は反復で得た進歩とそれを意味ある形で適用できる状況の両方を調べる。

sentences.en: The fictional music lesson suggests that changing the conditions of a practice activity can reveal questions that are difficult to ask when the learner is always permitted to begin in the same place.
sentences.ja: 架空音楽授業は練習条件を変えることで常に同じ箇所から開始できるときは問うのが難しい問いを明らかにし得ると示唆する。

questions.prompt: What problem does the teacher observe?
options: Students cannot play from the beginning at all.
Every student has stopped rehearsing.
Some students struggle when starting in the middle.
The piece becomes longer every week.
questions.explanation_ja: 途中からの演奏が難しい。

questions.prompt: Why does the teacher avoid dismissing their progress?
options: The students have already mastered every possible condition.
Success under familiar conditions remains a real achievement.
She knows changing practice is unnecessary.
She intends to stop assessing musical performance.

questions.prompt: What may have become a cue for starting a section?
options: The price of the musical instrument.
Reading an unrelated worksheet.
The end of the school day.
Completing the preceding section.
The same observed difficulty may have different causes.
Every pupil must depend on the same cue.
An observation proves a universal explanation.
Practice conditions cannot be altered.
questions.explanation_ja: 原因を一律に断定しない。

options: Repeating the piece only from its first measure.
Replacing all music with mathematics.
Removing all opportunities for full performance.
Starting at various points and recovering after interruptions.
questions.explanation_ja: 多様な開始位置と再開。

options: Partial practice never has any value.
Every interruption must be avoided.
A whole piece involves abilities not fully developed through isolated tasks.
Students should ignore the connections among sections.

questions.prompt: How might the distinction apply to mathematics?
options: All mathematical tasks involve musical cues.
Familiar exercises may not establish recognition of a concept in new problems.
A correct answer always proves flexible understanding.
Every worksheet should use the same questions.

questions.prompt: What is the limit of the analogy?
options: It does not establish one teaching method's effectiveness for all learners.
It cannot generate questions about practice.
It proves that all subjects are identical.
It demonstrates universal learning outcomes.
A repeated interruption.
A final examination score.
An underlying basis.
A replacement for every task.

questions.prompt: Which statement expresses the main argument?
options: Repeating a familiar task is always useless.
Successful performance requires eliminating all routines.
Starting a piece from the beginning is sufficient for every learning goal.
Practice should develop both performance in familiar settings and the ability to respond to changed conditions.

grammar.focus: than when they attempt them in isolation
grammar.explanation_ja: 比較級を用いた場面対比。

grammar.focus: since dividing a musical work into smaller tasks
grammar.explanation_ja: sinceは理由、動名詞句が主語。

grammar.focus: while leaving some aspects of independent performance
grammar.explanation_ja: while＋分詞で利点と限界を対比。

paraphrases.source: She recognizes that a procedure which produces successful performance under familiar conditions does not necessarily prepare students to respond when the conditions of a performance change.
paraphrases.rewrite: Success in familiar practice does not guarantee readiness for changed conditions.

paraphrases.source: Some students discover that the movements required at the beginning of one section are easier to recall when they have just completed the preceding section than when they attempt them in isolation.
paraphrases.rewrite: Movements may be easier after the previous section than on their own.

paraphrases.source: However, she continues to provide opportunities to perform the entire piece, since dividing a musical work into smaller tasks cannot by itself develop every aspect of a coherent performance.
paraphrases.rewrite: Full performances remain valuable because isolated exercises cannot develop every aspect of the work.

paraphrases.source: A familiar sequence can be an important foundation for learning while leaving some aspects of independent performance insufficiently developed.
paraphrases.rewrite: A repeated sequence can support learning without fully developing independent performance.
